results.question: How do tensor cores work?
results.response:
Tensor Cores are specialized compute units in NVIDIA GPUs that accelerate **matrix multiply-accumulate (GEMM)** operations—most efficiently when workloads are expressed in supported matrix sizes and data types. For example, in NVIDIA’s FP64 “Double-Precision Tensor Core” mode, a **single DMMA (double-precision matrix multiply-accumulate) job** uses **one instruction** to replace **eight traditional FP64 instructions**, so the GPU can complete the same matrix math with less work and better throughput. The Ampere-generation Tensor Cores also support larger matrix tiles (e.g., **8×8×4** vs **4×4×4** on Volta), which helps them handle tougher problems efficiently. Practically, CUDA and CUDA-X libraries expose these Tensor Core paths so applications can invoke the accelerated matrix math without manually coding the low-level instruction sequences.  

Sources:  
[1] What Is a Double-Precision Tensor Core? | NVIDIA Blog - https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/double-precision-tensor-cores/

scores.notes: Directly explains how Tensor Cores accelerate GEMM via matrix multiply-accumulate, mentions DMMA instruction reduction and tile size differences, and notes software exposure via CUDA libraries. However, only one source URL is provided and it’s unclear whether all specific claims (e.g., 8×8×4 vs 4×4×4) are supported by that citation. Overall consistent with common NVIDIA Tensor Core descriptions.
